---
title: "Set up Python"
subtitle: "About 10 minutes. Do it before the session if you can; we'll also do it together at the start."
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Stuck? Keep going in Colab

The install is the first 12 minutes of the session. Everything after it runs in Google Colab, in your browser, so a
stuck install won't hold you back: flag a helper and keep going. We'll finish it during the break.
:::

## 1. Open a terminal

A terminal is a window where you type commands instead of clicking.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

Press {{< kbd Cmd-Space >}}, type **Terminal**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

### Windows

Press the {{< kbd Win >}} key, type **PowerShell**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}. Your prompt starts with `PS C:\`.
:::

## 2. Install uv

uv is one small tool that installs Python and the packages you need. It needs no admin rights. Copy the line for your
computer, paste it into the terminal, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```
:::

### Windows (PowerShell)

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```
:::
:::

## 3. Check it worked

**Close the terminal and open a new one**, so it can find uv. Then run:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv --version
```
:::

You should see a version number, like `uv {{< var checked.uv >}}`.

## 4. Make the workshop folder

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv init --python {{< var python >}} --vcs none dss-python
cd dss-python
```
:::

- `--python {{< var python >}}` matches the Python that Colab uses, so code behaves the same in both places.
- `--vcs none` skips git, so a Mac without Apple's developer tools doesn't ask to install them.

## 5. Start JupyterLab

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab
```
:::

The first run downloads Python {{< var python >}} and JupyterLab. On shared Wi-Fi this is the slowest step, so give it
a few minutes. Then your browser opens JupyterLab.

1. Choose **New → Notebook**.
2. Type `1 + 1` in the first cell and press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}}.
3. You should see `2`.

To stop JupyterLab, go back to the terminal and press {{< kbd Ctrl-C >}} twice.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `uv: command not found` | Open a new terminal. Still missing on a Mac? Run `source $HOME/.local/bin/env`. |
| "running scripts is disabled" (Windows) | Use the exact command shown above, with `-ExecutionPolicy ByPass`. |
| Antivirus or SmartScreen blocks the install | Flag a helper, or ask at [go.ncsu.edu/getdatahelp]({{< var help >}}). |
| The browser didn't open | Copy the `http://localhost:…` link from the terminal and paste it into your browser. |
| The download is slow | Keep going in Colab. You can finish the install during the break. |

## 6. Open the notebook in Colab

Most of the session happens here.

1. Open the [learner notebook in Colab]({{< var colab.learner >}}).
2. Sign in with your Google account.
3. Click **Copy to Drive** in the toolbar.
4. Work in the new tab, titled **Copy of introduction-to-programming-with-python.ipynb**.

A "not authored by Google" warning means you're in the original tab. Switch to your copy.

## 7. Take your work home

In Colab, choose **File → Download → Download .ipynb**. Save it in your `dss-python` folder. Then, in the terminal:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
cd dss-python
uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab
```
:::

Open the notebook from JupyterLab's file list. The bar plot needs matplotlib. Stop JupyterLab, run
`uv add matplotlib`, and start it again.
